title: Work with coordinate frames
scope: SE(2), labelled transforms and point/direction semantics

items.prompt: Column vectors: T_AB maps B coordinates into A. Which transform maps B into A? Return T_AB or T_BA.
items.solution: The first subscript is the destination frame; the second is the source. Reverse direction uses the inverse.
hints: Identify the requested quantity and its units before calculating.
Write the equation using the supplied inputs, then check units and signs.
The first subscript is the destination frame; the second is the source. Reverse direction uses the inverse.
items.remediation: Compare one intermediate result with the stated model. Revisit /lessons/R03 or try the other scenario. This is a suggestion, not a diagnosis.

items.prompt: A transform rotates +π/2 then translates (2,2). Compute the transformed point p=(2,0) and direction v=(2,0), in that order. Return four coordinates.
items.solution: Both rotate to (0,2). Only the point receives translation.

items.prompt: Column vectors, T_AB maps B→A: T_AB is +π/2 rotation with translation (1,2); T_BC is pure translation (3,−1). Find the translation of T_AC=T_AB T_BC.
items.solution: Rotate (3,−1) to (1,3) then add (1,2): (2,5). Reversing order is not equivalent.
